app.title: Jidō Kundoku
app.tagline: Classical Chinese, read as Japanese. Paste a passage and get it marked up for reading aloud, with a plain Japanese version alongside.
main.empty: Enter text or upload a CoNLL-U file to begin.

help.title: Editing the analysis
help.intro: Each character is marked with its part of speech and with the character it attaches to. That analysis is what produces the reading order, the kaeriten and the kakikudashibun, so correcting it corrects all three at once.
help.step.select.title: Select a character
help.step.select.body: Click a character to pick it out. Right-click — or double-click, whichever comes easier — to see what the parse makes of it: its part of speech appears beneath it, and an arrow is drawn from the character it attaches to, labelled with the relation between them.
help.step.highlight.title: Follow it across
help.step.highlight.body: A character is never marked alone. Its reading is marked with it, and so is whatever it became in the kakikudashibun — which is not always the obvious word, since the reading order moves characters about and a kaeriten can carry one past its neighbours.
help.step.navigate.title: Move the selection
help.step.navigate.body: The arrow keys step from one character to the next along a line, and across to the next line — the two axes of vertical text. Escape lets the selection go.
help.step.pos.title: Change the part of speech
help.step.pos.body: Right-click or double-click the part of speech to choose another; the current one is marked. The reading follows from it, so both panels are redrawn at once — 中 as a verb is read ataru, as a noun naka. The chip is one of three, as the figure shows: resting the pointer on it slides out the two narrower categories the treebank records beside it — the semantic field and the sense — and each takes a menu of its own in the same way.
help.step.relation.title: Change the relation
help.step.relation.body: Right-click or double-click the label on the arrow to choose a different relation. This is what settles whether a character is read before the one it attaches to, and so whether it takes a kaeriten at all. A relation that has narrower kinds is written with them in brackets — 補語〖形式〗 — and each piece is picked on its own: the name before the bracket gives the plain relation, a word inside the bracket gives that narrower kind.
help.step.head.title: Attach it elsewhere
help.step.head.body: Drag a character onto the one it should attach to. A dashed line follows the pointer, and the character under it lights up as a candidate. On release the relation is renamed by the parser itself, which scores the new attachment just as it scored the original reading.
help.step.reading.title: Choose another reading
help.step.reading.body: Right-click or double-click the furigana for the other readings on offer — on'yomi first, and only those the part of speech admits. They are given in historical kana, as in the text itself. A saidoku moji is offered its two readings as one, written いまだ…ズ, and the second of them opens the same menu.
help.step.undo.title: Undo anything
help.step.undo.body: Every edit can be undone, including one that moved several characters at once. Hold Shift to redo. Edits stay with the text when you save it, and are written into the CoNLL-U file when you download it.
